Disabled Soviet nuclear submarine K-219 surfaces shortly before sinking with 34 nuclear warheads aboard. It still rests on the seafloor but several of the missiles are missing. North of Bermuda. 1986

K-219 was a Navaga-class ballistic missile submarine of the Soviet Navy. She carried 16 (later 15) SS-N-6 liquid-fuel missiles equipped with an estimated 34 nuclear warheads.

On Friday 3 October 1986, while on an otherwise routine Cold War nuclear deterrence patrol in the North Atlantic 680 miles (1,090 km) northeast of Bermuda, the 15-year-old K-219 suffered an explosion and fire in a missile tube. In an effort to control the results, the remains of a missile and its two warheads were ejected from its' silo into the sea. Two sailors were killed outright in the explosion, and a third died soon afterward from toxic gas poisoning. Through a breach in the hull, the vessel immediately started taking on sea water, quickly sinking from its original depth of 40 metres (130 ft) to eventually reach a depth in excess of 300 metres (980 ft) before being stabilized and surfacing. After attempts at towing the vessel failed, it began flooding again and and on 6 October 1986 the K-219 sank to the bottom of the Hatteras Abyssal Plain at a depth of about 6,000 m (18,000 ft).

In 1988, the Soviet research ship Keldysh positioned itself over the wreck and found the submarine sitting upright on the bottom but broken in two, aft of the conning tower. Several missile silo hatches had been forced open, and the missiles, along with the nuclear warheads they contained, were gone.
